title: By technician counts completed, comeback and warranty lines with the rate
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Have technician A for this test, who clocked time this month on exactly 4 lines now Complete.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B.
  • Have a new invoiced work order for this test, work order 4, for customer B, whose line 1 was done by technician A.
  • Have a new No Charge work order for this test, work order 1, for customer B, category Warranty, closed, closed this month, with 1.0 labor hour, 1 stock part at $80.00 and work order 4 as its original work order.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 2, for customer B, invoiced, billable, invoiced this month, whose line 2 of 1.5 hours was No Charge under Comeback with one stock part at $40.00 and work order 4's line 1 as its original line.
custom_steps:
1. Open Reports > Internal Work Orders.
  2. Set the date range to this month.
  3. Open the "By technician" tab.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The report opens.

Step 2:

  • The range is this month.

Step 3:

  • Technician A's row reads Completed lines 4, Comeback lines 1 (work order 2's line 2), Warranty lines 1 (work order 1 as a whole), Comeback rate 25% (1 ÷ 4).
  • Redo hours read 2.5 (1.5 + 1.0) and Redo parts cost $120.00 ($40.00 + $80.00).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S9-R2: “The report "Internal Work Orders" under Reports lists the closed internal and no-charge work orders of the organization and, one row each, the no-charge lines of invoiced billable work orders. Filters: date range on the posting or invoice date (default this month, at most 12 months), Location (all or one), Classification (All / Internal / No Charge / No Charge line), Category (All or one, archived under a heading), Original technician (All or one). Above the table a summary strip shows one card per category in the range: parts cost, count of work orders and lines, hours. Two tabs. "By work order and line", columns: Work order (link), Line ("Whole work order", or the line number and title), Customer, Classification, Category, Original work order (link, with the original line number when set), Original technician, Closed / invoiced (the posting date, or the invoice date for a line), Parts cost (one number: stock parts plus special orders and sublet, as on the NO CHARGE document, S3-R5; for a line, its own parts), Shop supplies (empty on a line), Hours (the labor hours on the lines, as on the document; clocked hours per technician are in Technician Efficiency with Only internal); a totals row for the whole range, not the page; rows sorted by date, newest first. "By technician", one row per technician with the columns Completed lines (lines with status Complete in the range on which the technician clocked time, the definition Technician Efficiency uses, so the two reports agree), Comeback lines and Warranty lines (no-charge lines of those categories whose stored original technicians include this technician, S2-R17), Comeback rate (comeback lines / completed lines), Redo hours and Redo parts cost (the hours and parts cost of that comeback and warranty work). A whole no-charge Comeback or Warranty work order counts as one line in this tab, with all its hours and parts cost. A line with several technicians counts once for each of them, in the numerator and the denominator, hours and cost shown whole for each; the totals row counts every line once; a note under the table says so. A row "Unassigned" holds the work without an original technician (Not in ShopView, or no technician on the original). The dollar cost of labor arrives with labor posting. Export: the PDF carries both tabs as sections with the same columns; the CSV carries the tab that is open, as every export gives what is on screen.”
  • S2-R17: “When the category requires the original work order, every dialog that sets the category (New Work Order S2-R2, Convert to No Charge S2-R5, Change category S2-R6, and the line dialogs of Story 12) shows the selects "Original work order" and "Original line" of S2-R2. Both are optional in the dialogs; the original work order is required at Close (S3-R2) and before Create invoice on a no-charge line (S12-R9); "Not in ShopView" satisfies it. The original technicians are derived when saved and stored with the work order or the line: every technician the original line shows, however they were assigned, by hand or from a schedule shift (a line with several technicians gives several, and the comeback counts once for each in the report); without an original line, the technician assigned to the original work order; without one, or with "Not in ShopView", none, and the report shows the job under Unassigned so it stays in the totals. They are shown in the dialog as soon as the original is picked, in the report (S9-R2) and in the hub record (S8-R1). The original work order is a link on the document, in the notes and in the report.”
  • Key Decisions: “The original work order and, optionally, the original line are stored with every Warranty and Comeback job, so the comeback and warranty numbers per technician come from data, not from a spreadsheet.”
  • Feature Overview: “Labor is hours only. The Internal Work Orders report gives hours per job, and Technician Efficiency with its chip on Only internal gives hours per technician, for a manual labor entry. Posting labor cost at technician pay is a later option.”
